result.rationale: The diff's server schema (addGuests.schema.ts) is z.array(z.string().email()) with no uniqueness refine, while AddGuestsDialog.tsx defines a refine requiring unique emails. The handler's uniqueGuests filter only excludes guests already in booking.attendees and blacklisted emails — it never dedupes within the input array — so ['a@x.com','a@x.com'] passes and createMany inserts duplicate attendee rows (or triggers a Prisma unique-constraint error surfaced as an untranslated INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR toast). This mismatch between client and server validation is a concrete, verifiable defect in the ad

adjudication.rationale: The client-side dialog defines a local ZAddGuestsInputSchema with a uniqueness `refine` (AddGuestsDialog.tsx) but the server-side ZAddGuestsInputSchema (addGuests.schema.ts) only validates `z.array(z.string().email())` with no uniqueness constraint. In the handler, `uniqueGuests` only filters against existing `booking.attendees` and blacklist (addGuests.handler.ts), and does not dedupe duplicates within the incoming `guests` array, so `['a@x.com','a@x.com']` can pass server validation and reach `createMany`. Whether this results in duplicate attendee rows or a DB constraint error depends on schema constraints not shown here, but the API accepting in-request duplicates and the client/server validation mismatch are directly verifiable from the diff.
